A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgentOCR study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are available and support reliable comparison despite pagination and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ALFWorld and search-QA evaluations, compression and caching experiments, self-compression ablations, and an appendix case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–4, Figure 3, and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the optical-history encoder, segment cache, compression action, success-conditioned logarithmic reward, intermittent reward schedule, and GRPO procedure. The prompt-tag corrections do not introduce an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six ALFWorld task categories and seven single-hop and multi-hop QA datasets. Their represented tasks and in-domain/out-of-domain coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Text (w/o RL), OCR (w/o RL), and Text + GRPO as comparators. The no-cache and naive-cache comparisons in Table 3 and self-compression controls in Table 4 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported search-QA prompts in Figures 6–7 correct malformed opening/closing tags for search, information, answer, and compression. This is a limited correction to the documented prompting protocol; other experimental settings remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Both retain the fixed-compression sweep in Figure 3, caching analysis in Table 3, self-compression and reward-schedule ablations in Table 4, and HotpotQA case study in Figures 8–9. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Point-estimate reporting and the least-squares cache-growth calculation in Table 3 are unchanged. Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched results in Tables 1–4, Figure 3, and the appendix case study are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains the 7B average QA scores of 40.1 for AgentOCR and 41.9 for Text + GRPO; Table 3 retains the 20.79× caching speedup.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, GRPO objective, Equations 1–8, and cache-complexity argument retain the same content. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about optical history, segment caching, and learned self-compression. Claims of preserving over 95% of text-agent performance, saving over 50% of tokens, and approximately 20× faster rendering remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of compression sensitivity, caching efficiency, and intermittent rewards are retained. Section 7 preserves the same limitations concerning backbone coverage, untested rendering choices, and reliance on predominantly textual histories.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository link on the first page and corrects control-tag documentation in Appendix B.5 and Figures 6–7. Existing pseudocode, hardware, training hyperparameters, and rendering parameters are retained; repository contents were not assessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kong et al. (2025), concerning token reduction in generative models, and cites it in Section 4's motivation. The related-work discussion and substantive novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited copyedits, including correcting 'AgenOCR,' changing 'Conclusion' to 'Conclusions,' and updating author/contact information. The prose, section order, and appendix organization are otherwise substantially retained.

P2.justification: Margins and display sizing change, Figure 2 is re-rendered with adjusted typography, and existing displays move with reflow. Table 3 shifts to page 10, while Figures 6–7 share a page in v2; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies a code-access pointer and repairs inconsistent prompt-tag examples in Appendix B.5 and Figures 6–7, reducing ambiguity for reproduction. The scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is a modest improvement in documentation and access guidance.
